subject: EU log routing split — new logging subprocessor & data residency question
messages:
From: EdgeStream Ops <ops@edgestream.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Proposed split of EU log routing — vendor details attached

Hi Mina,

Quick note — we plan to start routing log streams for our EU customers to a regional partner next month to reduce cross-border latency. The vendor is LogForge Ltd (UK), they would receive structured access logs and aggregated metrics.

High-level:
- Purpose: EU log ingestion and short-term troubleshooting (7–30 day retention window).
- Data types: service logs (timestamps, request paths, HTTP status), hashed identifiers; no raw prompt or model outputs should be knowingly forwarded.
- Location: primary endpoints in UK (London) with optional archival in our US backup if triggered.

Attached is their roster + a rough DPA draft from their side (LogForge_Roster_v1.pdf, logforge_dpa_draft.docx). Can you confirm if Redwood can accept LogForge as an EU subprocessor under our DPA and whether the proposed fallback archival to US would trigger additional controls?

We want to be transparent and get this finalized before we flip routing on June 1.

Thanks,
— Sam Carter
Ops Lead, EdgeStream
attachments: LogForge_Roster_v1.pdf (application/pdf), logforge_dpa_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeStream Ops <ops@edgestream.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed split of EU log routing — vendor details attached

Thanks Sam — quick acknowledgement. I'm looping in Security (Laura) and Compliance (Hannah) to validate the roster and the DPA draft. A few quick clarifying asks to speed review: 

1) Please confirm definitively whether any raw request/response payloads or model-generated tokens are included in the log stream. If any portion of prompt or model output flows to LogForge we need that documented.
2) What is the planned retention for the live pipeline and for backups? You mentioned 7–30 days but we need a single committed retention period per environment.
3) Encryption at rest and in transit? If they have their own KMS, who holds keys?
4) For the archival fallback to US — is that automatic or manual? If automatic, what triggers it and what controls will prevent unrelated customer data from being exported?

Laura / Hannah — please review the attached roster and the DPA draft; flag any missing SCCs, transfer mechanism, or additional contractual clauses (export controls, incident notification SLA).

I'll consolidate our list and get back to you with a short acceptance checklist within 48 hours.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: EdgeStream Ops <ops@edgestream.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: LogForge Legal <legal@logforge.co.uk>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:26:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed split of EU log routing — vendor details attached

Thanks — answers inline.

1) Data content: Logs are application-layer access logs and structured telemetry. We do not intend to forward raw prompt content or full model outputs. Some hashed identifiers and request metadata will be included.
2) Retention: Primary pipeline 14 days, debug snapshots (on demand) up to 90 days but require manual approval and are scoped to specific incidents.
3) Encryption: TLS in flight; encryption at rest using LogForge-managed keys (LogForge uses AWS KMS in eu-west-2). Keys are held by LogForge; they offered a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise customers if required.
4) Archival fallback: manual process triggered by support/ops for disaster recovery or eDiscovery; not automated. They have an approval workflow and access logging.

LogForge legal has attached a cleaner DPA draft (logforge_dpa_draft_v2.docx) and a short SOC2 summary.

Let us know if you need test endpoints or sample scrubs.

— Sam
attachments: logforge_dpa_draft_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), LogForge_SOC2_Summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed split of EU log routing — vendor details attached

Quick review notes after scanning the roster + DPA draft: 

- Positive: UK-based processing with TLS+KMS and manual archival workflow is preferable to fully automated cross-border replication.
- DPA gap: their draft does not include explicit Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or the UK Addendum language we require when a UK vendor may export to non-EEA territories — ask them to insert the latest UK SCCs and reference our DPA exhibit.
- Access controls: need clearer RBAC for support engineers (minimum privilege), and proof of per-access logging (who accessed which dataset and why).
- Incident notification: propose 24-hour breach notification for incidents affecting Redwood customer data; their draft currently says "reasonable efforts" — unacceptable.
- KMS: LogForge-managed keys are okay for standard customers, but for EdgeStream's tier we should require either customer KMS or a documented key-separation control and split access for archival retrieval.

Action items for legal & vendor: Markus to propose contract language for SCC/UK addendum and the 24-hour notification. Hannah to request SOC2 type II evidence for the last 12 months and run a brief vendor risk questionnaire about data minimization and pseudonymization.

Markus: ping for legal wording and whether we require an export license check given the backup-to-US scenario.

Laura
Director, Security Legal & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeStream Ops <ops@edgestream.io>, LogForge Legal <legal@logforge.co.uk>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:48:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed split of EU log routing — vendor details attached

Sam / LogForge team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the v2 DPA. To summarize Redwood's position and required next steps so there is no confusion: 

1) Data scope confirmation: EdgeStream to provide a sanitized sample (redacted) of the log schema within 48 hours confirming no raw prompt or model output. We will treat the presence of any prompt/model content as a blocker.
2) Retention: Commit to 14 days for the primary pipeline; any debug snapshots (up to 90 days) require a documented approval flow and must be itemized per incident. Please insert these commitments into the DPA.
3) Transfer mechanism: LogForge to add the current UK/EEA SCCs (and UK Addendum) into the DPA and explicitly document the manual archival process and approval gate that prevents automatic export.
4) KMS: For EdgeStream's account we require either a customer-managed KMS option or a written key-separation design and audit logs proving no Redwood plaintext access.
5) Incident and access controls: 24-hour notification SLA, RBAC proof, and per-access audit log exports in CSV for at least 90 days.

Please send updated DPA and SOC2 Type II evidence and the sanitized schema link to the Drive folder referenced above. If you can commit to providing the updated DPA and evidence by EOD May 14 we can greenlight a limited pilot with two EU customers on May 24 (controls-only pilot).

If any of the items above cannot be provided within that timeframe, let us know immediately so we can discuss mitigations.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
